---
title: "Fishing in the English Channel: Trends in Fishing Effort, Landings and Spatial distributions between countries and fleets"
subtitle: "A combined analysis using STECF AER, MMO, GFW and STECF FDI data (2008–2025)"
author: "Martin Pastoors"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
client: "Vrolijk"
output:
  word_document:
    reference_docx: "../report_template.dotx"
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
---


```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# ---- Check that the Word template exists ------------------------------------
# Must match reference_docx in the YAML header.
template_rel <- "../report_template.dotx"

# Pandoc resolves the path relative to the Rmd file, so check it from there.
# When chunks are run interactively, current_input() is NULL; fall back to
# the working directory.
rmd_dir <- if (!is.null(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))) {
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
} else {
  getwd()
}
template_path <- normalizePath(file.path(rmd_dir, template_rel), mustWork = FALSE)

if (!file.exists(template_path)) {
  stop("Word template not found: ", template_path,
       "\nCheck reference_docx in the YAML header, or copy the template to that location.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- Check that the output .docx can be overwritten -------------------------
# Pandoc fails at the very end of the knit if the previous output is still
# open in Word (Windows locks open files). Check this up front instead.
rmd_input <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)

if (!is.null(rmd_input)) {                     # only when knitting, not interactively
  out_docx <- file.path(rmd_dir,
                        sub("\\.[Rr]md$", ".docx", basename(rmd_input)))

  if (file.exists(out_docx)) {
    writable <- tryCatch({
      con <- file(out_docx, open = "ab")       # open for appending: writes nothing,
      close(con)                               # but fails if the file is locked
      TRUE
    }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)

    if (!writable) {
      stop("Output file is locked (probably open in Word): ", out_docx,
           "\nClose the document in Word and knit again.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

)

# ---- Years without UK (GBR) effort in the AER --------------------------------
# Used to place the asterisks in the effort figures. A year counts as missing
# when GBR has no fishing days in the study area in that year (over all gears).
gbr_missing_years <- function(effort, years = aer_years_start:aer_years_end) {
  gbr_years <- effort |>
    filter(sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer,
           country_code == "GBR",
           totfishdays  > 0) |>
    distinct(year) |>
    pull(year)

  setdiff(years, gbr_years)
}

# ---- Tables without a Total row ---------------------------------------------
# style_ft() formats the last row as a Total row. For tables without a Total
# row, this wrapper undoes that (the first column stays bold).
style_ft_plain <- function(ft, ...) {
  n_rows <- nrow(ft$body$dataset)
  style_ft(ft, ...) |>
    flextable::bold(i = n_rows, j = -1, bold = FALSE, part = "body") |>
    flextable::bg(i = n_rows, bg = "white", part = "body")
}

fig_nums("gfw_events_all",    paste0("Spatial distribution of GFW fishing events ",
                                      "(random sample of 20,000), all years combined, ",
                                      "coloured by country. ", study_area_lab, "."))
fig_nums("gfw_events_year",   paste0("Spatial distribution of GFW fishing events by year ",
                                      "(random sample of 10,000 per year), coloured by country. ",
                                      study_area_lab, "."))
fig_nums("kde_all",           paste0("Kernel density of GFW fishing effort for all fleets combined, ",
                                      "faceted by year. Bandwidth \u03c3 = ", sigma_all / 1000, " km. ",
                                      "Density normalised within each year (0 = low, 1 = high)."))
# Not used in this version (no figure chunk):
# fig_nums("kde_7d",            paste0("Kernel density of GFW fishing effort in ", focus_div_lab, ", all fleets combined, ",
#                                       "faceted by year. Bandwidth \u03c3 = ", sigma_7d / 1000, " km. ",
#                                       "Density normalised within each year (0 = low, 1 = high). ",
#                                       "Internal waters excluded."))
fig_nums("concentration",     paste0("Spatial concentration of GFW fishing effort in ",
                                      if (conc_scope == "full") study_area_lab else focus_div_lab, ": ",
                                      "Gini coefficient (left) and percentage of total effort in the ",
                                      "top-10% most-fished ", cell_size / 1000, " km grid cells (right), ",
                                      gfw_years_start, "\u2013", max(study_years), "."))

```{r load-aer}

# ---- AER effort and landings: all releases in aer_releases --------------------
# aer_effort_bysource / aer_landings_bysource : all releases, stacked (aer_source)
# aer_effort_raw / aer_landings_raw           : per country x year the release
#                                               with the highest priority
# aer_effort_summary, aer_effort_capacity_metric, aer_landings_summary
aer_objects <- c("aer_effort_bysource", "aer_landings_bysource",
                 "aer_effort_raw", "aer_effort_summary",
                 "aer_effort_capacity_metric",
                 "aer_landings_raw", "aer_landings_summary")

aer_source_files <- c(vapply(aer_releases, `[[`, "", "file"), div_cache)

if (cache_ok(aer_cache, aer_source_files, aer_objects)) {

  msg("AER: loading from cache (", format(file.mtime(aer_cache), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_cache)

} else {

  msg("AER: cache missing, stale or incomplete — reading releases ...")

  # ---- 1. Read each release ---------------------------------------------------
  effort_list   <- list()
  landings_list <- list()

  for (id in aer_priority) {
    rel <- aer_releases[[id]]
    msg("AER: reading ", rel$label, " ...")
    res <- read_aer_release(rel, study_divisions_aer)   # list(effort, landings)
    effort_list[[id]]   <- res$effort
    landings_list[[id]] <- res$landings
  }

  aer_effort_bysource   <- bind_rows(effort_list)
  aer_landings_bysource <- bind_rows(landings_list)

  # ---- 2. Combine: per country x year the release with the highest priority ----
  priority_labels  <- vapply(aer_releases[aer_priority], `[[`, "", "label")
  aer_effort_raw   <- combine_by_priority(aer_effort_bysource,   priority_labels)
  aer_landings_raw <- combine_by_priority(aer_landings_bysource, priority_labels)

  msg("AER combined: source per country (years):")
  aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, country_code) |>
    summarise(years = paste0(min(year), "–", max(year)), .groups = "drop") |>
    print(n = Inf)

  # ---- 3. Summaries -------------------------------------------------------------
  # Fishing days etc. per stratum (vessel_length kept for capacity plots)
  aer_effort_summary <- aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, year, country_code, gear_category, sub_reg, vessel_length) |>
    summarise(
      across(any_of(c("totfishdays", "totseadays", "totkwfishdays", "totgtfishdays")),
             ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # aer_effort_raw %>% filter(country_code=="NLD") %>% View()
  
  # GT-fishing days where reported; imputed from kW-fishing days otherwise
  aer_effort_capacity_metric <- aer_effort_summary |>
    mutate(
      gt_fishdays_source = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0 ~ "GT (reported)",
        totkwfishdays > 0 ~ "GT (imputed from kW)",
        TRUE              ~ "Not available"
      ),
      gt_fishdays_harmonised = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0 ~ totgtfishdays,
        totkwfishdays > 0 ~ totkwfishdays * kw_to_gt_ratio,
        TRUE              ~ NA_real_
      )
    )

  aer_landings_summary <- aer_landings_raw |>
    group_by(aer_source, year, country_code, gear_category,
             sub_reg, species_code, species_name) |>
    summarise(
      live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE),
      value_euro    = sum(value_euro,    na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # ---- 4. Save cache --------------------------------------------------------------
  save(list = aer_objects, file = aer_cache)
  msg("AER: cache saved → ", aer_cache)
  rm(effort_list, landings_list, res, rel)
}

```

```{r uk-share, include=FALSE}
# ---- UK share of landings (used in summary, results and conclusions) -------
# UK = GBR and Channel Islands, whatever the source: in 2020 the UK landings
# come from the AER (STECF 21-08), from 2021 onwards from MMO.
uk_share <- landings_combined_overlap |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(country_code %in% c("GBR", "CHI"), "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(fleet) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * t / sum(t))

uk_share_pct <- round(uk_share$pct[uk_share$fleet == "UK"])

uk_share_division <- landings_combined_overlap |>
  mutate(fleet = if_else(country_code %in% c("GBR", "CHI"), "UK", "EU")) |>
  group_by(fleet, sub_reg) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(sub_reg) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * t / sum(t))) |>
  ungroup()

uk_pct_div <- function(div) {
  uk_share_division$pct[uk_share_division$fleet == "UK" &
                        uk_share_division$sub_reg == div]
}

# ---- Spatial concentration metrics (used in summary, results, discussion) ----
# conc_scope (setup) selects the whole study area or the focus division.
if (conc_scope == "full") {
  conc_data     <- concentration_full
  conc_area_lab <- study_area_lab
} else {
  conc_data     <- concentration_7d
  conc_area_lab <- focus_div_lab
}

# Range of a vector as text, e.g. "0.53–0.57"; decimal = "," for the Dutch text
fmt_range <- function(x, digits, decimal = ".") {
  lo <- formatC(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = digits, decimal.mark = decimal)
  hi <- formatC(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), format = "f", digits = digits, decimal.mark = decimal)
  if (lo == hi) lo else paste0(lo, "\u2013", hi)
}

conc_years       <- sort(unique(conc_data$year))
conc_early_years <- head(conc_years, 4)        # first four years
conc_late_years  <- tail(conc_years, 5)        # last five years
conc_early_lab   <- paste0(min(conc_early_years), "\u2013", max(conc_early_years))
conc_late_lab    <- paste0(min(conc_late_years),  "\u2013", max(conc_late_years))

conc_early <- conc_data |> filter(year %in% conc_early_years)
conc_late  <- conc_data |> filter(year %in% conc_late_years)

conc_gini_early  <- fmt_range(conc_early$gini, 2)
conc_gini_late   <- fmt_range(conc_late$gini,  2)
conc_top10_early <- fmt_range(conc_early$top10_pct, 0)
conc_top10_late  <- fmt_range(conc_late$top10_pct,  0)
conc_peak_year   <- conc_data$year[which.max(conc_data$top10_pct)]
conc_peak_top10  <- round(max(conc_data$top10_pct, na.rm = TRUE))


```

<!-- =========================================================
     DOCUMENT BODY
     ========================================================= -->

---

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Executive summary
:::

Background and aim. The English Channel (`r study_area_lab`) is an intensively exploited fishing ground, with important fisheries for France, the United Kingdom, Belgium and the Netherlands. Over the past decade these fisheries have been shaped by two concurrent forces: changing fish stocks and post-Brexit access restructuring. Against this background, this report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk to provide an objective, evidence-based characterisation of fishing effort, landings and spatial distribution in the study area over the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (UK landings, MMO), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), with particular focus on the flyshoot segment.

Approach. Four complementary data sources were integrated: the STECF Annual Economic Report (AER; STECF 25-07 for the EU fleets and STECF 21-08 for the UK fleet up to `r aer_uk_years_end`), providing official fishing effort and landings by fleet segment; UK landings data from the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), covering UK and Channel Islands vessels, which are absent from the AER after `r aer_uk_years_end`; the STECF Fisheries Dependent Information database (FDI, STECF 25-10), used to disaggregate the AER bottom trawl/seine category into conventional otter trawl (OTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears; and Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-derived fishing event data, used for spatial analysis of effort distribution and concentration.

Key findings. Total fishing effort in the study area declined by approximately 30% between 2008 and 2023 (EU fleets only), driven primarily by contraction of French otter trawl fleet. France dominates the effort picture throughout, contributing around 63% of AER fishing days, with UK 34% van other countries 3% of fishing days between 2008 and 2020. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute terms, is the dominant seine fleet in the area, with approximately 70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days attributable to SSC/SDN gears. Landings are dominated by flatfishes and scallops **[CHECK: main species groups for 7.d/7.e]**. Flatfish landings declined by more than 60% since 2008, consistent with poor stock status for Channel sole and plaice. Scallop landings increased markedly since 2016, supported by record biomass in the Baie de Seine. 

Including the UK fleet. Over `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, UK and Channel Islands vessels accounted for around `r uk_share_pct`% of total landings in the study area (`r uk_pct_div(study_divisions_aer[1])`% in `r study_divisions_aer[1]` and `r uk_pct_div(study_divisions_aer[2])`% in `r study_divisions_aer[2]`). UK landings are dominated by shellfish (whelk, scallops, cockles and crab), taken mainly by pots and traps and dredges, together with horse mackerel, flatfish and cuttlefish. EU-only figures would therefore underestimate total landings in the study area by roughly 20% **[CHECK: recompute]**, and underrepresent shellfish and passive gears in particular. UK effort is available from the AER up to `r aer_uk_years_end`; for later years no UK effort data were available, so the effort trends from `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` onwards cover EU fleets only.

GFW spatial analysis reveals persistent fishing hotspots in the Pas de Calais and the Baie de Seine. Post-Brexit restructuring is visible from 2021 in the form of declining UK effort in 27.7.e and increasing spatial separation between national fleets. The spatial concentration of fishing effort in `r conc_area_lab` changed from a Gini coefficient of `r conc_gini_early` in `r conc_early_lab` to `r conc_gini_late` in `r conc_late_lab`, with a peak of `r conc_peak_top10`% of total effort concentrated in the top-10% of grid cells in `r conc_peak_year` **[CHECK: interpretation: structural shift?]**.

Conclusions. The fisheries in the Channel are undergoing a long-term structural contraction in effort, accompanied by declining landings of key flatfish species and progressive spatial concentration of the remaining fleet into a smaller number of heavily fished areas. The Dutch flyshoot fleet occupies a small but stable position within this system. The combination of AER, MMO, FDI and GFW data provides a robust multi-source baseline that can be used to contextualise the position of the Vrolijk fleet within the broader Channel fisheries, and to monitor future changes in fleet composition, spatial distribution and compliance with bilateral management arrangements.

::: {custom-style="Hheading 1"}
Nederlandse samenvatting
:::

Achtergrond en doel. Het Engelse Kanaal (`r study_area_lab`) behoort tot de meest intensief beviste wateren van Europa, met belangrijke visserijen voor Frankrijk, het Verenigd Koninkrijk, Bel-gië en Nederland. In het afgelopen decennium zijn deze visserijen beïnvloed door twee gelijktijdige ontwikkelingen: dalende visbestanden en herstructurering van de toegang na Brexit. In dit kader werd dit rapport in opdracht van Cornelis Vrolijk opgesteld, met als doel een ob-jectieve, op feiten gebaseerde beschrijving te geven van de visserij-inspanning, aanvoer en ruimtelijke verdeling in het studiegebied over de periode `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (Britse aanvoer, MMO), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI) en `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), met bijzondere aandacht voor het flyshoot-segment.

Aanpak. Vier complementaire databronnen zijn gecombineerd: het STECF Jaarlijks Economisch Rapport (AER; STECF 25-07 voor de EU-vloten en STECF 21-08 voor de Britse vloot tot en met `r aer_uk_years_end`) voor officiële visserij-inspanning en aanvoer per vlootsegment; aanvoergegevens van de Britse Marine Management Organisation (MMO) voor Britse vaartuigen en vaartuigen van de Kanaaleilanden, die na `r aer_uk_years_end` ontbreken in de AER; de STECF Fisheries Dependent Information-database (FDI, STECF 25-10) om de AER-categorie "bordenvisserij/zegen" te splitsen in conventionele bordenvisserij (OTB) en flyshoot (SSC/SDN); en Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-gebaseerde visserijdata voor ruimtelijke analyse.

Belangrijkste bevindingen. De totale visserij-inspanning in het studiegebied daalde met circa 30% tussen 2008 en 2023 **[CHECK: herberekenen]**, voornamelijk door inkrimping van de Franse bordenvisserij (OTB) en de Belgische en Nederlandse boomkorvis-serij. Frankrijk domineert het gehele inspanningspatroon en levert circa 80% van de AER-visdagen. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot is in absolute termen klein, maar is de dominante zegenvisserij in het gebied: circa 70% van de Neder-landse bordenvisserij/zegen-visdagen is toe te schrijven aan zegentuigen (SSC/SDN). De aanvoer wordt gedomineerd door platvis en sint-jakobsschelpen. De aanvoer van platvis daalde met meer dan 60% ten opzichte van 2008, consistent met de slechte bestandsstatus van tong en schol in het Kanaal. De aanvoer van sint-jakobsschelpen nam sterk toe na 2016, gesteund door recordbiomassa in de Baie de Seine.

Britse vloot. In `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)` was de Britse vloot (inclusief de Kanaaleilanden) goed voor circa `r uk_share_pct`% van de totale aanvoer in het studiegebied, (`r uk_pct_div(study_divisions_aer[1])`% in `r study_divisions_aer[1]` en `r uk_pct_div(study_divisions_aer[2])`% in `r study_divisions_aer[2]`). De Britse aanvoer bestaat vooral uit schelpdieren en schaaldieren (wulken, sint-jakobsschelpen, kokkels en krab), gevangen met potten en fuiken en dreggen, aangevuld met horsmakreel, platvis en zeekat. Cijfers die alleen op de AER zijn gebaseerd onderschatten de totale aanvoer in het studiegebied daardoor met ongeveer 20%. Britse inspanningsgegevens zijn in de AER beschikbaar tot en met `r aer_uk_years_end`; voor latere jaren ontbreken ze, zodat de inspanningstrends vanaf `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` alleen EU-vloten betreffen.

De GFW-ruimtelijke analyse laat persistente visserijhotspots zien in het Nauw van Calais en de Baie de Seine. De gevolgen van Brexit zijn zichtbaar vanaf 2021: de Britse inspanning in 27.7.e neemt af en de nationale vloten vissen steeds meer in afzonderlijke gebieden. De ruimtelijke concentratie in `r conc_area_lab` veranderde van een Gini-coëfficiënt van `r fmt_range(conc_early$gini, 2, ",")` in `r conc_early_lab` naar `r fmt_range(conc_late$gini, 2, ",")` in `r conc_late_lab`, met een piek waarbij `r conc_peak_top10`% van de totale inspanning was geconcentreerd in 10% van de rastercellen in `r conc_peak_year`.

Conclusies. De visserij in het Kanaal ondergaat een langdurige structurele krimp in inspan-ning, gepaard met dalende aanvoer van belangrijke platvissoorten en toenemende ruimtelijke concentratie van de resterende vloot. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot neemt een kleine maar stabiele positie in binnen dit systeem. De combinatie van AER-, MMO-, FDI- en GFW-data biedt een robuuste, meervoudige databasis die kan worden ingezet om de positie van de Vrolijk-vloot te contextualiseren binnen de bredere Channel-visserij, en om toekomstige veranderingen in vloot-samenstelling, ruimtelijke verdeling en naleving van bilaterale beheersafspraken te monitoren.


# Introduction

## Background

This study looks into the international fisheries developments in the English Channel in the past 15 years. Over this period there has  been an increase in the fisheries for squid and cuttlefish in the Channel (and more recently also in the Southern North Sea). This change in fishing patterns has come under increasing public and media scrutiny, including critical coverage in the Netherlands (e.g. Follow the Money). This study attempts to provide a thorough knowledge base on the Channel fisheries using data from different sources: 1) STECF Annual Economic Report (AER; STECF 21-08 and 25-07; STECF, 2021, 2025a), 2) UK landings data `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (MMO, 2025), 3) STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI; STECF, 2025b) and 4) Global Fishing Watch data (https://globalfishingwatch.org). The aim is to provide an objective, evidence-based assessment of the fisheries development in terms of effort and catches of fleets operating in the Channel and the available scientific literature on those fisheries.

The report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk company (https://www.cornelisvrolijk.eu) and executed by Martin Pastoors Fish & Fisheries.  

## Objectives

- To quantify trends in fishing effort and landings in the Channel (2008/2013–present) using official STECF (AER) and MMO statistics, with spatial distribution characterised using GFW AIS data.
- To compile a scientifically grounded overview of the fisheries in the Channel, with particular focus on sustainability, ecosystem effects and the positioning of the flyshoot fishery.

## Study area and scope

The study covers `r study_area_text`. The combination of these divisions will be called "study area" in the report.

```{r study-area-map, fig.height=6.5, fig.width=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("study_area")}

# ---- Study area map: ICES divisions, countries and water depth ---------------
# Depth: NOAA ETOPO 2022 global relief model at 1 arc-minute (~1.8 km),
# downloaded once with marmap::getNOAA.bathy() (needs an internet connection
# and the marmap package: install.packages("marmap")).
# The depth grid is stored in cache_map.RData, together with the map window
# it was downloaded for; it is downloaded again when map_xlim / map_ylim change.
# ICES division outlines: fao_sf_context (load-divisions chunk).
# The map window (map_xlim / map_ylim) follows from the study divisions plus
# map_buffer_deg (setup); uncomment the two lines below to set it by hand.
#
# EEZ boundaries: Marine Regions World EEZ v12 boundary lines (Flanders Marine
# Institute, 2023). Either set eez_file to a local copy of the boundaries
# layer (e.g. "eez_boundaries_v12.shp" from https://www.marineregions.org/downloads.php),
# or leave it NULL to download the layer once with the mregions2 package
# (install.packages("mregions2")). Stored in cache_eez.RData.

map_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_map.RData")
# map_xlim       <- c(-8, 3)         # longitude range of the map
# map_ylim       <- c(47.5, 51.3)    # latitude range of the map
show_windfarms <- TRUE             # draw operational/approved wind farms
eez_cache      <- file.path(cache_dir, "cache_eez.RData")
eez_file       <- NULL             # optional local EEZ boundaries file (shp/gpkg)

# ---- Depth grid (NOAA ETOPO) ----------------------------------------------------
bathy_df    <- NULL
map_cache_ok <- FALSE

if (file.exists(map_cache)) {
  load(map_cache)   # bathy_df, bathy_xlim, bathy_ylim
  # Only valid if it was downloaded for the same map window
  map_cache_ok <- exists("bathy_xlim") && exists("bathy_ylim") &&
                  isTRUE(all.equal(bathy_xlim, map_xlim)) &&
                  isTRUE(all.equal(bathy_ylim, map_ylim))
  if (map_cache_ok) {
    msg("Map: depth grid loaded from cache")
  } else {
    msg("Map: map window has changed — depth grid is downloaded again")
    bathy_df <- NULL
  }
}

if (!map_cache_ok) {

  msg("Map: downloading depth grid from NOAA ...")
  bathy_df <- tryCatch({
    b <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(lon1 = map_xlim[1] - 0.5, lon2 = map_xlim[2] + 0.5,
                               lat1 = map_ylim[1] - 0.5, lat2 = map_ylim[2] + 0.5,
                               resolution = 1)
    marmap::fortify.bathy(b)                 # columns x (lon), y (lat), z (m)
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: depth download failed (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without depth and the download is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  if (!is.null(bathy_df)) {
    bathy_xlim <- map_xlim
    bathy_ylim <- map_ylim
    save(bathy_df, bathy_xlim, bathy_ylim, file = map_cache)
    msg("Map: cache saved → ", map_cache)
  }
}

# ---- ICES divisions in the map window --------------------------------------------
# fao_sf_context (load-divisions) holds all divisions around the study area
ices_div_map <- fao_sf_context

# ---- EEZ boundaries ------------------------------------------------------------
if (file.exists(eez_cache)) {

  load(eez_cache)   # eez_lines

} else {

  eez_raw <- tryCatch({
    if (!is.null(eez_file)) {
      msg("Map: reading EEZ boundaries from ", eez_file)
      sf::st_read(eez_file, quiet = TRUE)
    } else {
      msg("Map: downloading EEZ boundaries from Marine Regions (first knit only) ...")
      mregions2::mrp_get("eez_boundaries")
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    msg("Map: EEZ boundaries not available (", conditionMessage(e),
        "); the map is drawn without EEZs and this is retried next knit.")
    NULL
  })

  eez_lines <- NULL
  if (!is.null(eez_raw)) {
    s2_old <- sf::sf_use_s2()
    sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
    eez_bbox <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = map_xlim[1] - 1, xmax = map_xlim[2] + 1,
                                            ymin = map_ylim[1] - 1, ymax = map_ylim[2] + 1),
                                          crs = 4326))
    eez_lines <- eez_raw |>
      sf::st_transform(4326) |>
      sf::st_make_valid() |>
      sf::st_intersection(eez_bbox) |>
      dplyr::select(geometry)
    sf::sf_use_s2(s2_old)
    rm(eez_raw)
    save(eez_lines, file = eez_cache)
    msg("Map: EEZ cache saved → ", eez_cache)
  }
}

# EEZ names: fixed label positions (lon, lat); adjust if labels overlap.

The period of analysis is `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` for effort and landings trends (AER; data for 2024 were not available for France and 2024 has therefore been left out; the UK fleet is included up to `r aer_uk_years_end`), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` for UK landings (MMO), and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` for spatial analysis (GFW).



# Material & Methods

This report combines four data sources, each covering a different period and providing different information. `r fig_nums("data_overview", display="cite")` gives an overview: the AER provides the long-term series of EU effort and landings, the MMO data add the landings of the UK and Channel Islands fleets from 2020 onwards, the FDI data are used only to split the AER bottom trawl/seine category into otter trawl and seine, and the GFW data are used only for the spatial analysis. The sources are described in detail in Sections `r sec["aer"]`–`r sec["gfw"]`.

## STECF AER data (effort and landings trends)

The Annual Economic Report (AER) data were obtained from two STECF data releases (*EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data, fleet segment level*): STECF 25-07 (STECF, 2025a), covering the EU Member States for `r min(aer_releases$aer2025$years)`–`r max(aer_releases$aer2025$years)`, and STECF 21-08 (STECF, 2021), the last release that includes the United Kingdom, covering `r min(aer_releases$aer2021$years)`–`r max(aer_releases$aer2021$years)`. The 25-07 release is used for every country × year combination it contains; the 21-08 release only adds the UK fleet. The AER provides fishing effort (fishing days, sea days, kW-days, GT-days) and landed weight and value by fleet segment (country × fishing technique × vessel length class), disaggregated by FAO division. 

The AER analyses in this report cover the period **`r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`**. The end year of 2023 reflects the absence of French effort and landings data for 2024 in the current STECF 25-07 release. The AER does not distinguish between bottom trawl and seine fisheries; they are reported as a combined category. 

After `r aer_uk_years_end` the AER no longer contains data for the United Kingdom. UK landings for the later years were therefore obtained separately from the UK Marine Management Organisation (Section `r sec["uk"]`). No UK effort data were available for the years after `r aer_uk_years_end`, so from `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` onwards the effort figures cover EU fleets only; years without UK effort are marked with an asterisk in the effort figures.


### Vessel length classes

The AER reports effort and landings by vessel length class (VLC), defined by overall length (LOA) in metres. Six standard classes are used throughout this report, as defined in the STECF fleet data collection framework:

```{r vlc-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  `Code`              = c("VL0010","VL1012","VL1218","VL1824","VL2440","VL40XX"),
  `Length range (m)`  = c("< 10","10–12","12–18","18–24","24–40","> 40"),
  `Typical vessel type` = c(
    "Small inshore vessels (outboard/inboard motor)",
    "Small coastal vessels",
    "Medium coastal/demersal vessels",
    "Medium offshore vessels, beam trawlers, flyshoot",
    "Large demersal and pelagic trawlers",
    "Freezer trawlers"
  )
) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 9) |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = tab_nums("vlc_table",
      "Vessel length classes (VLC) used in STECF AER data and throughout this report.")
  )
```

VL0010 and VL40XX are included in data tables but excluded from some effort figures where their small contribution makes them difficult to display alongside the dominant VL1218–VL2440 classes. All classes are included in the Annex D tables.

### Species groups

Landings in the AER are reported at the individual species level using FAO 3-alpha species codes. For summary figures and tables, individual species are aggregated into ecologically and commercially meaningful species groups. The grouping was applied using FAO 3-alpha codes as the primary key (reliable and consistent across member states) with species name pattern matching as a fallback. `r tab_nums("spp_group_table", display="cite")` lists the species groups used and the main constituent species.

## UK landings data (MMO)

UK landings were obtained from the dataset underlying the UK Sea Fisheries Statistics 2024 (MMO, 2025), covering landings by UK vessels into all ports and landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports for 2020–2024. The dataset reports monthly landings by vessel nationality, ICES division and statistical rectangle, port of landing, vessel length group, gear category and species, as live weight, landed weight and first-sale value (GBP).

**Selection.** Only vessels of UK nationality (England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland) were retained, together with vessels from Jersey and Guernsey, which are reported separately as Channel Islands (CHI). Landings by non-UK vessels into UK ports were excluded, because these are already included in the AER data of the respective flag states. The data were restricted to `r study_area_lab`.

**Harmonisation with the AER.** UK vessel length groups were mapped onto the AER vessel length classes (`r tab_nums("vlc_table", display="cite")`) using the lower bound of each length group. UK gear categories were mapped onto the AER gear categories as shown in `r tab_nums("uk_gear_map", display="cite")`. The original UK gear categories were retained in addition; unlike the AER, they distinguish demersal trawls from demersal seines. Species are coded with FAO 3-alpha codes in both sources, but some species are reported under different codes. Horse mackerel (HOM/JAX), cuttlefish (CTC/CTL), monkfish (ANF/MON/MNZ), squids (SQC/SQR/SQZ) and skates and rays (RJx/SKA) were therefore harmonised to a common code before species grouping (Section `r sec["spp"]`). Live weight was used throughout, consistent with the AER. Values were converted from GBP to EUR using annual average ECB exchange rates.

**Use and limitations.** The MMO data cover landings only. They are added only for the country × year combinations that are not in the AER, i.e. from `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` onwards; for `r aer_uk_years_end` and earlier the UK landings come from the AER (STECF 21-08), so nothing is counted twice. UK landings before and after `r aer_uk_years_end + 1` therefore come from different sources, which may differ somewhat in coverage. UK effort is only available from the AER, up to `r aer_uk_years_end`. Direct comparisons between EU and UK landings are restricted to `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, the years covered by both the EU and the UK data. Spatial attribution may differ slightly between sources: UK landings are attributed to the reported rectangle and division, while AER landings by sub-region are compiled by Member States from logbook and sales-note data.

```{r uk-gear-map-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(

                               "Dredge", "Drift and fixed nets",
                               "Handlines, Longlines", "Pots and traps",
                               "Pelagic seine",
                               "Pelagic trawls, Other mobile/passive gears, Unknown"),
  `AER gear category`      = c("Bottom trawl/seine", "Bottom trawl/seine", "Beam trawl",
                               "Dredge", "Gillnet",
                               "Handline/rod", "Pot/trap",
                               "Purse seine",
                               "Other/mixed")
) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 9) |>
  flextable::set_caption(caption = tab_nums("uk_gear_map"))
```


## STECF FDI data — limitations and use as gear-splitting key

The STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI) dataset was obtained for the study area and period. Unfortunately the FDI Landings table is EU-aggregated (no country breakdown) and the Effort and Catches tables suffer from substantial confidentiality suppression in many strata. In addition, the spatial FDI tables were not available on the STECF website at the time of analysis. Therefore, the FDI data has not been used as the main source of the data for the report. 

Despite these limitations, the FDI Effort table retains one piece of information not available in the AER data: **gear code at the FAO level** (e.g. OTB, OTT, SSC, SDN, PTB). The AER combines all of these into a single `Bottom trawl/seine` category, which conflates conventional otter trawl (OTB) with Danish/Scottish seine (SSC/SDN), two gears with very different fishing patterns and fleet compositions. The FDI gear-code information is therefore used to disaggregate the AER `Bottom trawl/seine` category, as described below.

**Splitting approach.** For each stratum `(year, country, vessel length class, division)`, the share of each gear code within the `Bottom trawl/seine` total was computed from the FDI Effort table. This proportional split key was then applied to the corresponding AER fishing days, so that the total days in each stratum are conserved exactly. Shares in the FDI strata are rescaled to sum to 1 within each stratum, handling any within-stratum confidentiality suppression transparently.

**Coverage and fallback rules.** FDI data are used for `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` only. Post-2013 strata with no FDI coverage (primarily IRL, DNK, and some BEL and DEU strata where FDI reported zero or suppressed days) are assigned a pooled fallback split key derived from the FDI data aggregated across all available years and countries, stratified by vessel length class.

**Limitations.** Countries for which FDI coverage is sparse (IRL, DNK, DEU) receive a pooled fleet-average split that may not reflect their actual gear mix. Results for these countries should be interpreted with caution and are excluded from the figures showing the French and Dutch trends.

## GFW data (spatial effort distribution and concentration)

Fishing activity data were retrieved via the Global Fishing Watch (GFW) API (`gfwr` v3.0) using the Events endpoint. Vessel metadata (country, gear type, gross tonnage) were obtained from the GFW vessel registry (https://globalfishingwatch.org; Kroodsma et al., 2018).

Recent publications have shown that the haul-based effort from GFW may not be a reliable indicator of fishing effort for trawl-based gears (Hintzen et al., 2025). Therefore, we define GFW days at sea in this report as vessel-days: for each day, each vessel is assigned to the ICES division in which it spent the majority of its time, based on the spatial distribution of AIS positions recorded during that day. This definition is therefore a simple presence-day metric. The effort trends derived from GFW data were found to be very different from effort trends in AER (and FDI) data. An important limitation of the GFW data is that vessels below the AIS carriage requirement threshold (typically 15 m LOA, though requirements vary by country and fishing area) are systematically under-represented or absent. This means that gears dominated by small inshore vessels — gillnets, pots and traps, handlines — are structurally under-counted relative to larger trawl and seine vessels, which carry AIS as a mandatory requirement. Therefore, the GFW data are used exclusively for the spatial analysis using effort density maps, spatial hotspots, and effort concentration metrics. The GFW spatial analysis covers the full period `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)`.

### Kernel density estimation of spatial effort distribution

The spatial distribution of fishing effort was characterised using kernel density estimation (KDE), a standard non-parametric method for converting a set of discrete point locations into a smooth continuous surface representing effort intensity (Silverman, 1986). For each year, fishing event coordinates were projected into a metric coordinate system (UTM Zone 30N) and a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km was applied across the full study area. The bandwidth is fixed across years so that changes in the density surface reflect genuine shifts in fishing distribution rather than smoothing artefacts. Land is excluded from the estimation window. The resulting surface is normalised to a 0–1 scale within each year, making spatial patterns directly comparable across years regardless of differences in total effort; for absolute effort levels, the AER-based effort figures in Section `r sec["effort"]` should be consulted alongside the KDE maps. KDE is widely used in fisheries spatial analysis to identify persistent hotspots, characterise seasonal grounds and detect shifts in fleet distribution over time (Gerritsen & Lordan, 2011; Kroodsma et al., 2018).

### Spatial concentration metrics: Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share

Two complementary metrics were computed annually for `r if (conc_scope == "full") study_area_lab else focus_div_lab` on a regular `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid to quantify how concentrated fishing effort is in space, rather than simply where it occurs. The Gini coefficient is a well-established inequality measure — originally from economics and widely applied in fisheries spatial analysis (Greenstreet et al., 2009; Eigaard et al., 2017) — that summarises the full distribution of effort across all grid cells on a scale from 0 (effort perfectly uniform across all cells) to 1 (all effort in a single cell). Values above approximately 0.7 indicate strong spatial concentration; a rising Gini over time signals progressive compression of effort into fewer areas, which may reflect displacement from previously accessible grounds, regulatory closures or increasing targeting efficiency. The top-10% cell share is a more intuitive companion metric: it expresses what percentage of total annual fishing events falls within the 10% of grid cells that were most intensively fished that year. If effort were uniform this would equal 10%; values of 40–70% are typical in concentrated demersal fisheries. Together the two metrics capture different aspects of concentration — the Gini reflects the shape of the full distribution while the top-10% share highlights the intensity of the most-fished areas — and tracking both annually allows changes in spatial footprint to be detected even when total effort remains stable.

## Literature review approach

The literature review underpinning Section `r sec["literature"]` draws on four categories of sources:

**Scientific literature** was identified through targeted searches of Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar using the terms: *English Channel fisheries*, *Channel demersal fisheries*, *flyshoot*, *Danish seine Channel*, *beam trawl North Sea Channel*, *scallop Pecten maximus Channel*, *seabed disturbance trawl*, *AIS fishing effort*, and combinations thereof. Priority was given to peer-reviewed articles published since 2010, supplemented by earlier foundational studies where relevant (e.g. Eigaard et al., 2017; Depestele et al., 2016).

**ICES working group reports** were sourced from the ICES library (https://www.ices.dk), primarily:

- *Working Group on Celtic Seas Ecoregion* (WGCSE, ICES 2025a) — principal source for demersal stocks in the Channel (sole, plaice, whiting, sea bass, monkfish, megrim, mullet) and for the broader ecosystem and fisheries context of 27.7.d/e.
- *Working Group on the Assessment of Demersal Stocks in the North Sea and Skagerrak* (WGNSSK, ICES 2025c) — consulted for stocks with distributions spanning the Channel (e.g. plaice, dab, horse mackerel).
- *Working Group on Widely Distributed Stocks* (WGWIDE, ICES 2025e) — responsible for the assessment of mackerel (*Scomber scombrus*) and horse mackerel (*Trachurus trachurus* western stock), both of which can be important bycatch species in the study area.
- *Working Group on Cephalopod Fisheries and Life History* (WGCEPH, ICES 2025d) — consulted for cuttlefish (*Sepia officinalis*) and squid (*Loligo* spp., *Illex* spp.) in the Channel and North Sea. WGCEPH does not produce formal TAC advice but provides the best available science on stock status and drivers of variability.
- *Working Group on Ecosystem Effects of Fishing Activities* (WGECO) — for seabed disturbance and ecosystem-level assessments.

ICES advice sheets for the relevant stocks were also consulted directly.

**Official statistics and national sources** include the STECF AER (primary quantitative source for this report), Ifremer fleet and stock assessment reports, the UK Marine Management Organisation (MMO) annual sea fisheries statistics, and the Belgian ILVO annual fleet reports. Where possible, the most recent published edition was used.

**Policy and grey literature** includes EU regulation texts, the UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement fisheries annex, and parliamentary reports on post-Brexit fisheries.

All quantitative claims made in the literature sections are cross-referenced with the AER and GFW results presented in Section `r sec["results"]`, and discrepancies or gaps are noted where they arise.

# Results

## Landings trends

### Landings by species during `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`

The overall landings by species in the study area (`r study_area_lab`) during all of the years available in the AER & MMO data are shown in the figure below. Scallops, herring and tangle (seaweed) have the highest landings. France and the UK are dominating the landings of scallops, The Netherlands and Germany are dominating landings of herring and France is responsible for the landings of tangle.  

```{r aer-landings-top-species, fig.height=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_top20")}

# ---- Top 20 species by total landed weight, AER + MMO, by country -------------
# Species are grouped on the harmonised code (species_code_harm), so species
# that the AER and MMO code differently (e.g. HOM/JAX) are counted together.
# Years are limited to the AER period, so all countries cover the same years.

top_years     <- aer_years_start:aer_years_end
top_countries <- unique(report_countries_combined)

top_data <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year    %in% top_years) |>
  mutate(country_code = if_else(country_code %in% top_countries,
                                country_code, "Other"))

# One name per harmonised code: the most frequent name in the data
top_names <- top_data |>
  count(species_code_harm, species_name_harm, wt = live_weight_t) |>
  group_by(species_code_harm) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(species_code_harm, species_name_harm)

# Top 20 species over all countries
top_species <- top_data |>
  group_by(species_code_harm) |>
  summarise(total_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total_t, n = 20) |>
  left_join(top_names, by = "species_code_harm") |>
  mutate(species_label = paste0(species_name_harm, " (", species_code_harm, ")"))

plot_top <- top_data |>
  filter(species_code_harm %in% top_species$species_code_harm) |>
  group_by(species_code_harm, country_code) |>
  summarise(total_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(top_species |> dplyr::select(species_code_harm, species_label, species_total = total_t),
            by = "species_code_harm") |>
  mutate(species_label = fct_reorder(species_label, species_total),
         # countries ordered by their total, largest first; "Other" last
         country_code  = fct_reorder(country_code, total_t, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE),
         country_code  = fct_relevel(country_code, "Other", after = Inf))

# Colours: flag_colours where defined, extra colours for any other country
extra_cty   <- setdiff(levels(plot_top$country_code), names(flag_colours))
cty_colours <- c(flag_colours,
                 setNames(c("#EDC948", "#9C755F", "#FF9DA7", "#499894")[seq_along(extra_cty)],
                          extra_cty))

ggplot(plot_top, aes(x = total_t / 1000, y = species_label, fill = country_code)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cty_colours, name = "Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title    = "Top 20 species by total landed weight, all gears",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  ", min(top_years), "\u2013", max(top_years)),
       caption  = paste0("AER (", aer_source_lab, "); UK landings after ", aer_uk_years_end,
                         " and Channel Islands (CHI) from MMO."),
       x = "Total landed weight (1000 t)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title      = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

```

Tangle (LQD) is a seaweed species being harvested from the sea (*Laminaria digitata*). Common European bittersweet (GKL) is a shellfish species (*Glycymeris glycymeris*).


### Total landed weight by year, country and gear

Total landings by gear and country are shown in the figure below. Highest landings are in the category Other/mixed which includes pelagic trawl (for e.g. herring). Beam trawl, bottom trawl/seine and dredge are the three gear types that generate somewhat comparable amounts of landings. Beam trawl is dominated by the Netherlands and bottom trawl/seine and dredge by France. 

```{r aer-landings-total, fig.height=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_gear")}

# ---- Landed weight by year, gear category and country, AER + MMO --------------
gear_countries <- unique(report_countries_combined)

plot_gear <- landings_combined |>
  # remove_pelagic_anomaly() |>
  filter(country_code  %in% gear_countries,
         sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% report_gears_aer) |>
  mutate(data_source = if_else(str_detect(source, "MMO"), "MMO", "AER")) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, gear_category, data_source) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year, country_code, gear_category, fill = list(live_weight_t = NA_real_)) |>
  mutate(country_code  = factor(country_code,  levels = gear_countries),
         gear_category = factor(gear_category, levels = report_gears_aer))

# Colours: flag_colours where defined, extra colours for any other country
extra_cty   <- setdiff(gear_countries, names(flag_colours))
cty_colours <- c(flag_colours,
                 setNames(c("#EDC948", "#9C755F", "#FF9DA7", "#499894")[seq_along(extra_cty)],
                          extra_cty))

gear_years <- range(plot_gear$year)

ggplot(plot_gear, aes(x = year, y = live_weight_t,
                      colour = country_code, group = country_code)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = aer_uk_years_end + 0.5, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = data_source), size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cty_colours, drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70",
                      name = "Country") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(AER = 16, MMO = 1), na.translate = FALSE,
                     name = "Source") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(gear_years[1], gear_years[2], by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  # facet_wrap(~gear_category, scales = "free_y") +
  facet_wrap(~gear_category) +
  labs(title    = "Landed weight by gear category and country",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  AER (", aer_source_lab, ") and MMO"),
       caption  = paste0(c(paste0("Dashed line: UK landings from the AER up to ", aer_uk_years_end,
                                  ", from MMO afterwards (open points)."),
                           pelagic_anomaly_note), collapse = "\n"),
       x = "Year", y = "Landed weight (t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text      = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box      = "horizontal",
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1),
         shape  = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

```


### Total landed weight for Other/mixed gear by year, country and species group

The `Other/mixed` gear category covers a highly diverse range of fishing techniques and target species that do not fit neatly into the main AER gear categories. The composition of this category differs markedly by country. French `Other/mixed` landings are dominated by seaweeds (tangle LQD and kelp LAH, harvested mechanically from the seabed) and pelagic fish (herring, mackerel, sardine and horse mackerel), together accounting for over 60% of French `Other/mixed` volume throughout the series. The increase in French `Other/mixed` landings since 2019 — visible in the preceding landings-by-gear figure — is driven largely by growing seaweed harvests rather than increasing pelagic or demersal fishing activity. Dutch, UK and German `Other/mixed` landings are almost entirely pelagic fish. Belgian `Other/mixed` landings are negligible at this scale and have been omitted.

```{r aer-landings-species-country-groups, fig.height=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_spp_grp_cty")}

# ---- Other/mixed gear: landings by species group and country, AER + MMO --------
# Countries with less than min_share_pct of the Other/mixed landings are left out,
# because their bars would not be visible at this scale.
min_share_pct <- 1

om_data <- landings_combined |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category == "Other/mixed",
         country_code  %in% unique(report_countries_combined)) |>
  mutate(species_group = assign_species_group(species_code_harm, species_name_harm),
         species_group = replace_na(species_group, "Other"),
         species_group = factor(species_group, levels = c(species_group_levels, "Other")))

om_countries <- om_data |>
  group_by(country_code) |>
  summarise(t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * t / sum(t)) |>
  filter(pct >= min_share_pct) |>
  arrange(desc(t)) |>
  pull(country_code)

om_years <- range(om_data$year)

plot_om <- om_data |>
  filter(country_code %in% om_countries) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, species_group) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year = om_years[1]:om_years[2], country_code, species_group,
           fill = list(live_weight_t = 0)) |>
  mutate(country_code = factor(country_code, levels = om_countries))

ggplot(plot_om, aes(x = year, y = live_weight_t / 1000, fill = species_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_group_colours, name = "Species group", drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(om_years[1], om_years[2], by = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~country_code, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title    = "Other/mixed gear: landings by species group and country",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  ", om_years[1], "\u2013", om_years[2]),
       caption  = paste0("AER (", aer_source_lab, "); UK after ", aer_uk_years_end,
                         " and Channel Islands from MMO. Countries with less than ",
                         min_share_pct, "% of Other/mixed landings not shown. "),
       x = "Year", y = "Landed weight (1000 t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

```

### Key species groups — landings by country

Landings in the study area are dominated by flatfishes and scallops in terms of volume, with flatfish landings showing a marked decline from around 40,000 t in 2008 to below 15,000 t by 2023, driven almost entirely by the Dutch (NLD) and Belgian (BEL) fleets **[CHECK: numbers and countries for 7.d/7.e]**. This is consistent with the contraction of beam trawl effort over this period. Scallop landings are dominated by France (FRA) and show an increasing trend since 2016, reaching record levels in 2022–2023. Cephalopod landings (cuttlefish and squid) are France-dominated and show moderate interannual variability. Landings of mackerel, horse mackerel, whiting, mullets and gurnards are comparatively low across all countries.

```{r aer-landings-species-country, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_spp_cty")}

# AER + MMO landings; species grouped on the harmonised species codes
spp_countries <- unique(report_countries_combined)

plot_data_cty <- landings_combined |>
  filter(country_code  %in% spp_countries,
         sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         year          <= aer_years_end) |>
  mutate(species_group = assign_species_group(species_code_harm, species_name_harm)) |>
  filter(!is.na(species_group),
         species_group != "Shrimps") |>                 # negligible in the study area
  group_by(year, country_code, species_group) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t=sum(live_weight_t, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  complete(year, country_code, species_group, fill=list(live_weight_t=0)) |>
  mutate(country_code  = factor(country_code, levels=spp_countries),
         species_group = factor(species_group, levels=species_group_levels)) 
  # Set entire 2012 Pelagic fish bar to NA — anomaly makes year unreliable
  # mutate(live_weight_t = if_else(
  #   year == 2012 & species_group == "Pelagic fish",
  #   NA_real_, live_weight_t))

# asterisk_cty <- data.frame(
#   species_group = factor("Pelagic fish", levels=species_group_levels),
#   year          = 2012,
#   label         = "*"
# )

ggplot(plot_data_cty, aes(x=year, y=live_weight_t, fill=country_code)) +
  geom_col(position="stack", width=0.8, na.rm=TRUE) +
  # geom_text(data=asterisk_cty, aes(x=year, y=0, label=label),
  #           inherit.aes=FALSE, vjust=-0.3, size=5,
  #           colour="red", fontface="bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=flag_colours, drop=FALSE, na.value="grey70",
                    name="Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(aer_years_start, aer_years_end, by=2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
  facet_wrap(~species_group, ncol=4) +
  labs(title    = "Landings by key species group and country",

                         " and Channel Islands from MMO."),
       x="Year", y="Landed weight (t)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
        strip.text   = element_text(size=7),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.caption = element_text(size=6.5, colour="grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

### Key species groups — landings by gear category

The gear breakdown confirms that flatfish landings are almost entirely taken by beam trawl, with a steep decline since 2008. Scallops are dominated by dredge. ## Effort trends (STECF AER)

### Total fishing days by year and country (all gears)

Total fishing effort in the study area declined from around 235,000 days in 2008 to approximately 160,000 days in 2023, a reduction of roughly 30% over the period. France consistently dominates total effort, accounting for approximately 80% of fishing days throughout the series **[CHECK: recompute; GBR is now included up to 2020, which creates a step in the totals in 2021]**. The Netherlands is the second largest contributor, with effort relatively stable over the period. Belgian and German effort is small and declining. The overall downward trend is driven primarily by reductions in French effort, with a notable step-down around 2019–2020 that may partly reflect COVID-19 disruption as well as post-Brexit access restrictions in subsequent years.

```{r aer-effort-country-total, fig.height=5, fig.cap=fig_nums("effort_country")}

# Stacking order from the bottom up; all other countries are grouped as "Other"
stack_order <- c("FRA", "NLD", "DEU", "BEL", "Other", "GBR")

effort_cty <- 
  aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year    <= aer_years_end) |>
  mutate(country_code = if_else(country_code %in% stack_order, country_code, "Other")) |>
  group_by(year, country_code) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(year = aer_years_start:aer_years_end,
           country_code = stack_order,
           fill = list(totfishdays = NA_real_)) |>
  mutate(country_code = factor(country_code, levels = stack_order))

#   summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% 
#   ungroup() %>% 
#   mutate(pct = totfishdays / sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE)) %>% 
#   print()

# effort_cty %>% 
#   filter(country_code != "GBR") %>%  
#   group_by(year) %>%
#   summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
#   ungroup() 

# effort_cty %>% 
#   filter(year <= 2020) %>%  
#   group_by(country_code, year) %>%
#   summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
#   ungroup() %>% 
#   View()


# Years without UK data: asterisk above the total of that year
gbr_missing <- effort_cty |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(total   = sum(totfishdays, na.rm = TRUE),
            gbr_na  = all(is.na(totfishdays[country_code == "GBR"]) |
                          totfishdays[country_code == "GBR"] == 0),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(gbr_na)

ggplot(effort_cty, aes(x = year, y = totfishdays, fill = country_code)) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(data = gbr_missing, aes(x = year, y = total, label = "*"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 6,
            colour = "red", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = flag_colours, drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey70",
                    name = "Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = aer_years_start:aer_years_end,
                     limits = c(aer_years_start - 0.5, aer_years_end + 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)),
                     labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title    = "AER: Fishing days by year and country",
       subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  All gears combined"),
       caption  = if (nrow(gbr_missing) > 0)
                    paste0("* No UK (GBR) effort data in ",
                           paste(range(gbr_missing$year), collapse = "\u2013"),
                           " (not in the AER after ", aer_uk_years_end, ")."),
       x = "Year", y = "Fishing days") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey40")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

```

### Total fishing days by year, country and gear category

The breakdown of effort by gear category reveals that the dominant gears in the study area are bottom trawl/seine, dredge, gillnet and pot/trap, with the `Other/mixed` category contributing a substantial and growing share in 27.7.d (see Section `r sec["landings_om"]` for further analysis of that category). Bottom trawl/seine effort is predominantly French throughout, with a gradual declining trend. Dredge effort is almost exclusively French, reflecting the scallop fleet operating in 27.7.d and 27.7.e. The Dutch fleet is most visible in beam trawl and, to a lesser extent, `Other/mixed`. Belgian effort appears primarily in beam trawl and shows the strongest decline of any national fleet over the period.

### Total fishing days by year, country and vessel length class

Fishing effort by vessel length class reveals distinct fleet structures by country. The French fleet (FRA) dominates across the smaller vessel size classes, with the largest absolute number of fishing days in the smaller vessel classes (VL0010–VL1218). This reflects the broad size distribution of the French demersal fleet. French effort shows a gradual declining trend across most size classes over the period. The Dutch fleet (NLD) is concentrated in the medium-to-large vessel classes (VL1824 and VL40XX), consistent with the flyshoot and beam trawl fleet composition, and shows relatively stable effort over time. Belgian effort (BEL) is most visible in the VL1824 class and shows a clear declining trend, consistent with the contraction of the Belgian beam trawl fleet documented in the landings data. German effort (DEU) is negligible across all size classes. Notably, the VL1824 class shows the most multi-country competition for effort, with French, Dutch and Belgian vessels all active in this size range.

### Disaggregation of bottom trawl/seine into OTB and SSC/SDN (FDI-derived)

As described in Section `r sec["fdi"]`, the AER Bottom trawl/seine category was disaggregated into conventional otter trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears using proportional split keys derived from the STECF FDI Effort data. The left panel shows that the category is heavily dominated by conventional bottom trawl throughout 2013–2023, with overall fishing days declining by over 30% over the period. The right panel shows the gear-type share based on direct FDI splits only: conventional otter trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 85–90% of days, with seine (SSC/SDN) contributing 10–15% and showing a modest upward trend in its share towards the end of the period. The picture varies strongly by country: France is almost exclusively OTB (~96%), while the Netherlands is predominantly seine (SSC/SDN, ~70%), reflecting the Dutch flyshoot fleet composition. Note that BEL and DEU received pooled fallback splits due to sparse FDI coverage and are therefore excluded from the percentage panel.


```{r aer-split-trend, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("split_total")}

if (!is.null(aer_split)) {

  split_2colours <- c(
    "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)" = "#E15759",
    "Seine (SSC/SDN)"             = "#4E79A7"
  )

  # Years without any UK (GBR) effort data, over all gears
  gbr_missing_yr <- gbr_missing_years(aer_effort_summary)

  # ---- Left panel: absolute fishing days ---------------------------------------
  abs_data <- aer_split |>
    filter(year <= aer_years_end,
           gear_type != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(fishdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(gear_type = factor(gear_type, levels = names(split_2colours)))

  abs_missing <- abs_data |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(total = sum(fishdays), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(year %in% gbr_missing_yr)

  p_abs <- ggplot(abs_data, aes(x = year, y = fishdays, fill = gear_type)) +
    geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = abs_missing, aes(x = year, y = total, label = "*"),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.2, size = 6,
              colour = "red", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = split_2colours, name = NULL,
                      guide = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(aer_split_years_start, aer_years_end, by = 2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)),
                       labels = scales::label_comma()) +
    labs(subtitle = "Absolute fishing days", x = "Year", y = "Fishing days") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x   = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))

  # ---- Right panel: gear share (FDI direct splits only) -------------------------
  pct_data <- aer_split |>
    filter(year         %in% aer_split_years_start:aer_years_end,
           split_source == "FDI direct",
           gear_type    != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(totdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(year) |>
    mutate(pct = round(100 * totdays / sum(totdays), 0)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(gear_type = factor(gear_type, levels = names(split_2colours)))

  pct_missing <- tibble::tibble(
    year = intersect(gbr_missing_yr, unique(pct_data$year))
  )

  p_pct <- ggplot(pct_data, aes(x = year, y = pct, colour = gear_type, group = gear_type)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")),
              vjust = -0.8, size = 2.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(data = pct_missing, aes(x = year, y = 0),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 8, size = 1.8, stroke = 0.8,
               colour = "red") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = split_2colours, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(aer_split_years_start, aer_years_end, by = 2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08)),
                       labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(subtitle = "Gear share (%) \u2014 FDI direct splits only",
         x = "Year", y = "Share of fishing days (%)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
          plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))

  p_abs + p_pct +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title    = "AER \u2014 Bottom trawl/seine disaggregated by gear code",
      subtitle = paste0(study_area_lab, "  \u2014  FDI gear-code split applied to AER fishing days"),
      caption  = if (length(gbr_missing_yr) > 0)
                   paste0("* No UK (GBR) effort data in ",
                          paste(range(gbr_missing_yr), collapse = "\u2013"),
                          " (not in the AER after ", aer_uk_years_end, ")."),
      theme    = theme(
        plot.title      = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        plot.caption    = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey40"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
      )
    )

} else {
  cat("aer_split not available.\n")
}


```

## Global Fishing Watch (GFW) effort data and comparison with AER

### Total GFW fishing days by year and country

GFW-derived fishing effort in the study area shows a clear increasing trend from around 53,000 days in 2013 to approximately 90,000 days in 2024–2025, contrasting with the declining trend seen in the AER data. Unlike the AER-based figures after `r aer_uk_years_end`, the GFW series includes the United Kingdom (GBR), which accounts for approximately 25–30% of total effort in the area and is the second largest contributor after the Netherlands **[CHECK: numbers for 7.d/7.e]**. The size class breakdown shows that effort is dominated by small vessels (S1 <100 GT), with a growing contribution from this class driving much of the overall increase. French and Dutch effort appears relatively stable in the GFW series, suggesting the overall increase may partly reflect improving AIS coverage over time rather than a genuine increase in fishing activity.

### AER vs GFW effort comparison

The two data sources measure effort differently: AER reports administrative fishing days declared by member states; GFW estimates fishing days from AIS vessel-tracking. The comparison below shows total fishing days over the overlapping period `r gfw_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`. The AER series covers `r paste(aer_countries_comparison, collapse = ", ")` only, because UK effort is in the AER only up to `r aer_uk_years_end`; the GFW series covers `r paste(if (gfw_like_for_like) aer_countries_comparison else report_countries_gfw, collapse = ", ")`.

Several factors can explain systematic differences between the two series:

- **Method for counting fishing days**: AER records one fishing day as any day on which a vessel is registered as fishing by its country; GFW counts a vessel-day as active when AIS-derived speed and movement patterns are classified as fishing behaviour. The two methods can disagree for the same vessel on the same day.
- **AIS coverage and adoption**: AIS was gradually mandated across the EU fleet between 2008 and 2014. Early years of the GFW series therefore under-represent vessels that did not yet carry AIS transponders, leading to lower GFW effort estimates before ~2014.
- **Small coastal vessels**: Vessels below ~15 m LOA are not required to carry AIS in many jurisdictions. This segment is captured in the AER (via logbook reporting) but largely absent from GFW, causing a structural undercount in GFW relative to AER for gears dominated by small vessels (e.g. pot/trap, gillnet).
- **Gear type assignment**: GFW classifies gear from AIS movement patterns; misclassification can shift effort between gear categories when comparing with AER gear-specific totals.
- **Spatial attribution**: AER effort is attributed to the ICES division declared in the logbook; GFW effort is attributed to the GPS position of the fishing event. In boundary areas the two can differ.

```{r aer-gfw-comparison, fig.height=5, fig.cap=fig_nums("aer_gfw_compare")}
# AER countries: aer_countries_comparison (setup; GBR left out because UK
# effort is in the AER only up to aer_uk_years_end).
# GFW countries: the same countries when gfw_like_for_like = TRUE (setup),
# otherwise all report_countries_gfw (incl. GBR).
if (gfw_like_for_like) {
  gfw_countries_comparison <- aer_countries_comparison
} else {
  gfw_countries_comparison <- report_countries_gfw
}
comparison_years <- gfw_years_start:aer_years_end

aer_label <- paste0("AER (", paste(aer_countries_comparison, collapse="+"), ")")
gfw_label <- paste0("GFW (", paste(gfw_countries_comparison, collapse="+"), ")")

aer_total <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(country_code %in% aer_countries_comparison,
         sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year         %in% comparison_years) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(fishing_days=sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  mutate(source=aer_label)

gfw_total <- fishing_days_study |>
  filter(vessel_flag %in% gfw_countries_comparison,
         year        %in% comparison_years) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(fishing_days=sum(fishing_days), .groups="drop") |>
  mutate(source=gfw_label)

bind_rows(aer_total, gfw_total) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=fishing_days/1000, colour=source, shape=source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth=1) + geom_point(size=2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=comparison_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=setNames(c("#E15759","#4E79A7"), c(aer_label, gfw_label))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values=setNames(c(16L, 17L), c(aer_label, gfw_label))) +
  labs(title    = "Effort comparison: AER vs GFW",
       subtitle = study_area_lab,
       x="Year", y="Fishing days (1000)", colour="Source", shape="Source") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1), legend.position="bottom") +
  guides(colour=guide_legend(nrow=1), shape=guide_legend(nrow=1))

### Spatial distribution of GFW fishing events

The spatial distribution of GFW fishing events reveals clear national zoning patterns across the study area. French (FRA) effort dominates the eastern and western Channel (27.7.d/e), spread broadly across the divisions. UK (GBR) effort is distributed throughout the Channel, with particular concentration in 27.7.e.

```{r gfw-plot-spatial-all, fig.height=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("gfw_events_all")}

From 2021 onwards, the spatial separation between national fleets becomes more pronounced, suggesting reduced overlap in fishing grounds following the EU-UK TCA access arrangements.
