### Kernel density in the study area

Kernel density estimation (KDE) converts the discrete set of fishing event locations into a continuous surface representing the spatial intensity of fishing effort. For each year, fishing event coordinates are projected into a metric coordinate system (UTM zone 30N) and a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km is applied within the study area boundary (land excluded). The resulting density surface is normalised within each year to a 0–1 scale, where 1 represents the grid cell with the highest density and 0 the lowest. This within-year normalisation makes annual maps directly comparable in terms of spatial pattern, but means that absolute effort levels cannot be compared between years, a year with low total effort and a year with high total effort will both have cells reaching 1.0. For absolute effort comparisons, refer to `r fig_nums("gfw_flag_total", display="cite")` and `r fig_nums("aer_gfw_compare", display="cite")`.

The KDE maps corroborate and sharpen the patterns visible in the point distribution maps above. In the Channel, the eastern entrance to 27.7.d around the Pas de Calais consistently shows the highest effort density, reflecting the concentration of French bottom trawl activity in this area. A notable feature emerging from around 2021–2022 is the relative weakening of the 27.7.e density signal, particularly in the northern (UK) portion of the division, reinforcing the post-Brexit reduction in UK fleet activity suggested by the point maps. The KDE representation also makes clear that while the spatial footprint of fishing appears broadly stable across the series, the intensity within hotspot areas has increased relative to background effort levels — a pattern that will be quantified further by the concentration metrics in the following section.

```{r gfw-plot-kde, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("kde_all")}


ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_tile(data=kde_results %>% filter(year >= gfw_years_start + 1), aes(x=x, y=y, fill=ndensity)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="inferno", name="Relative\ndensity",
                       limits=c(0,1), breaks=c(0,0.5,1),
                       labels=c("Low","Mid","High"), na.value="transparent") +
  geom_sf(data=world_proj, fill="grey85", colour="grey60", linewidth=0.2) +
  geom_sf(data=fao_div_proj, fill=NA, colour="grey30", linewidth=0.4) +
  coord_sf(crs=crs_proj,
           xlim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")],
           ylim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")],
           expand=TRUE) +
  theme(axis.text=element_blank(), axis.ticks=element_blank(),
        axis.title=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom",
        strip.background=element_rect(fill="grey90"),
        strip.text=element_text(face="bold", colour="grey20")) +
  labs(title=paste0("GFW: Fishing effort density, all fleets (σ = ", sigma_all/1000, " km)"),
       subtitle="Normalised per year  —  Land excluded") +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol=3)


```

```{r gfw-plot-kde-7d-country, fig.height=8, fig.width=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("kde_7d_country")}

# ---- GFW KDE by country, before and after Brexit -----------------------------------
# Density as a share of each period's events (density_share), so that the panels
# show where each fleet fishes, independent of the number of years in a period
# and of the growth in AIS-recorded events over time.

kde_flags <- c("FRA", "GBR", "NLD")

# Periods: labels and year ranges
kde_periods <- list(
  "2013\u20132019" = 2013:2019,
  "2020\u20132025" = 2020:2025
)

# ---- Events in the study area for the selected flags --------------------------
# Flag from vessel_meta, as in the other GFW chunks
events_study <- events_classified_fr |>
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("vessel_flag", "vessel_name"))) |>
  left_join(vessel_meta |> dplyr::select(vesselId, vessel_flag), by = "vesselId") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(lubridate::year(start))) |>
  filter(division    %in% study_divisions_gfw,
         vessel_flag %in% kde_flags,
         year        %in% unlist(kde_periods))

# msg("KDE by period: ", nrow(events_study), " events after filtering")

# Project to UTM 30N
events_study_sf <- events_study |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(crs_proj)

# ---- KDE per period x flag, all years within a period pooled -------------------
kde_list   <- list()
kde_counts <- list()

for (period in names(kde_periods)) {
  for (flag in kde_flags) {

    yrs <- kde_periods[[period]]
    pts <- events_study_sf |>
      filter(vessel_flag == flag,
             year        %in% yrs)

    if (nrow(pts) < 20) {
      msg("KDE by period: ", period, " ", flag, ": only ", nrow(pts), " events, skipped")
      next
    }

    coords  <- st_coordinates(pts)
    ppp_obj <- spatstat.geom::ppp(
      x      = coords[, 1],
      y      = coords[, 2],
      window = study_owin            # points outside the window are dropped
    )
    n_points <- spatstat.geom::npoints(ppp_obj)   # events inside the study window

    kde_raw <- spatstat.explore::density.ppp(
      ppp_obj,
      sigma    = sigma_all,
      dimyx    = c(200, 200),
      positive = TRUE
    )

    kde_list[[paste(period, flag)]] <- as.data.frame(kde_raw) |>
      rename(density = value) |>
      mutate(period        = period,
             vessel_flag   = flag,
             # share of the period's events per unit area (sums to 1 over the area)
             density_share = density / n_points)

    kde_counts[[paste(period, flag)]] <- tibble::tibble(
      period      = period,
      vessel_flag = flag,
      n_points    = n_points,
      n_years     = length(yrs)
    )

    msg("KDE by period: ", period, " ", flag, ": ", n_points, " events")
  }
}

kde_study_grid <- bind_rows(kde_list)
kde_n          <- bind_rows(kde_counts)

# ---- Normalise within each country (shared scale across the two periods) --------
kde_study_grid <- kde_study_grid |>
  group_by(vessel_flag) |>
  mutate(ndensity = (density_share - min(density_share, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                    (max(density_share, na.rm = TRUE) - min(density_share, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(vessel_flag = factor(vessel_flag, levels = kde_flags),
         period      = factor(period,      levels = names(kde_periods)))

# ---- Number of events per panel, as a label in the top-left corner ----------------
study_bbox <- st_bbox(study_window_proj)

kde_n_labels <- kde_n |>
  mutate(vessel_flag = factor(vessel_flag, levels = kde_flags),
         period      = factor(period,      levels = names(kde_periods)),
         label       = paste0("n = ", format(n_points, big.mark = ","), " events"),
         x           = study_bbox[["xmin"]] + 0.02 * (study_bbox[["xmax"]] - study_bbox[["xmin"]]),
         y           = study_bbox[["ymax"]] - 0.04 * (study_bbox[["ymax"]] - study_bbox[["ymin"]]))

# ---- Plot ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = kde_study_grid,
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = ndensity)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option   = "inferno",
    name     = "Relative density",
    limits   = c(0, 1),
    breaks   = c(0, 0.5, 1),
    labels   = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = world_proj,   fill = "grey85",
          colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = fao_div_proj, fill = NA,
          colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_label(data = kde_n_labels,
             aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
             hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2.6,
             fill = alpha("white", 0.8), label.size = 0) +
  coord_sf(crs  = crs_proj,
           xlim = study_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")],
           ylim = study_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
           expand = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(vessel_flag ~ period) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("GFW: Fishing effort density by country and period",
                      " (\u03c3 = ", sigma_all / 1000, " km)"),
    subtitle = paste0(
      study_area_lab, "  \u2014  Density as share of each period's events, ",
      "normalised within each country\n",
      "Colour scale shared across periods for each country; independent of the ",
      "number of years and events per period"
    ),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text        = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9))

```



## GFW effort spatial concentration: Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share

Two complementary metrics are used to quantify the spatial concentration of fishing effort across the `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid cells covering `r conc_area_lab`.

The **Gini coefficient** is a standard inequality measure borrowed from economics, adapted here to quantify the unevenness of effort across grid cells. It ranges from 0 to 1: a value of 0 means fishing effort is spread perfectly uniformly across all cells; a value of 1 means all effort is concentrated in a single cell. In practice, fishing effort is always somewhat concentrated. Values above 0.7 indicate strong spatial concentration in a small number of areas, while values below 0.5 suggest a relatively dispersed fleet. A rising Gini over time indicates that the fleet is progressively concentrating in fewer locations.

The **top-10% cell share** is a more intuitive companion metric: it asks what percentage of the total annual fishing events falls within the 10% of grid cells that were most intensively fished that year. If effort were uniform, this would be exactly 10%. In practice values of 40–70% are common in concentrated fisheries, meaning that a small fraction of the available sea area absorbs the majority of fishing pressure. Together, the two metrics capture different aspects of spatial concentration: the Gini summarises the full distribution of effort, while the top-10% share focuses specifically on the most intensively exploited areas.

The Gini coefficient for `r conc_area_lab` ranged from `r conc_gini_early` in `r conc_early_lab` to `r conc_gini_late` in `r conc_late_lab`. The proportion of total effort in the most-fished 10% of cells was `r conc_top10_early`% in `r conc_early_lab` and `r conc_top10_late`% in `r conc_late_lab`, with a peak of `r conc_peak_top10`% in `r conc_peak_year`. **[CHECK: the interpretation below was written for the 27.7.D metrics; revise for the values above]** Together these metrics quantify what the KDE maps suggested qualitatively — that while the broad spatial footprint of fishing has remained relatively stable, effort has become increasingly concentrated within already-intensively-fished areas. The peak in concentration around 2019–2020 coincides with a period of significant fleet restructuring driven by post-Brexit access uncertainty and the COVID-19 pandemic. The partial relaxation of concentration since 2021 may reflect fleets settling into new access arrangements under the EU-UK TCA, though values remain consistently above the pre-2018 baseline, pointing to a structural rather than purely temporary shift in spatial behaviour.

```{r gfw-plot-concentration, fig.height=4, fig.cap=fig_nums("concentration")}

# conc_data: whole study area or focus division, see conc_scope in setup
p_gini <- ggplot(conc_data, aes(x=year, y=gini)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(colour="#E15759", linewidth=1) + geom_point(colour="#E15759", size=3) +
  geom_text(aes(label=round(gini,2)), vjust=-0.8, size=2.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=study_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), labels=scales::number_format(accuracy=0.01)) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.5)) +
  labs(x="", y="Gini coefficient", title="Gini coefficient")

p_top10 <- ggplot(conc_data, aes(x=year, y=top10_pct)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(colour="#4E79A7", linewidth=1) + geom_point(colour="#4E79A7", size=3) +
  geom_text(aes(label=paste0(round(top10_pct,0),"%")), vjust=-0.8, size=2.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=study_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,100),
                     labels=scales::percent_format(scale=1)) +
  # scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,100), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.15)),
  #                    labels=scales::percent_format(scale=1)) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.5)) +
  labs(x="", y="% of total effort", title="Top-10% cell share")

p_gini + p_top10 +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = paste0("GFW: Effort concentration ", conc_area_lab, "  \u2014  ",
                      cell_size/1000, " km grid  \u2014  All fleets"),
    subtitle = "Left: Gini coefficient (0=uniform, 1=fully concentrated). Right: % effort in top-10% cells.")
```

## Channel fisheries context: literature review

This section places the quantitative results from Sections `r sec["landings"]`–`r sec["concentration"]` in the broader context of the Channel fisheries literature. It draws on ICES WGCSE, STECF, Ifremer, MMO and peer-reviewed sources (see Section `r sec["lit_methods"]` for the literature selection approach).

### Fleet composition and dominant gear types

The Channel (ICES 27.7.d/e) supports one of the most diverse and intensively fished areas in Europe. The French fleet dominates total effort in the eastern Channel, contributing over 60% of total AER fishing days in most years (ICES, 2025a; Ifremer, 2026) **[CHECK: align with the AER share in Section `r sec["effort_country"]`]**, consistent with the AER results in `r fig_nums("effort_gear_cat", display="cite")`, which show France as the largest contributor across all gear categories. Bottom trawl/seine gears account for the largest share of demersal fishing effort, targeting mixed assemblages of flatfish, cephalopods and small pelagics. The Dutch flyshoot fleet expanded through the 2010s (Quirijns et al., 2020), a trend visible in the AER and GFW series (`r fig_nums("split_fra_nld", display="cite")` and `r fig_nums("gfw_flag_total", display="cite")`). Belgian beam trawl effort has declined substantially since the mid-2000s under pressure from fuel costs and quota restrictions (Departement Landbouw en Visserij, 2022), consistent with the low and declining Belgian effort in beam trawl panels throughout the AER figures.

The scallop dredge fishery is concentrated in the Baie de Seine (27.7.d) and western Channel (27.7.e), dominated by the French fleet with seasonal UK participation. Scallop landings from the Baie de Seine reached a record ~48,000 t in 2024–2025 (Varenne & Foucher, 2025) **[CHECK: landings or survey biomass?]**. MSC certification has been granted for the Baie de Saint-Brieuc fishery (2022) and the Baie de Seine fishery (November 2024), covering the majority of French Channel scallop production (MSC, 2024). The landings data (`r fig_nums("landings_top20", display="cite")`, Figures `r fig_nums("landings_spp_cty", display="num")`–`r fig_nums("landings_spp_gear", display="num")`) confirm scallops as one of the highest-tonnage species in the study area, dominated by the French dredge fleet.

Pot and trap fisheries targeting whelk (*Buccinum undatum*), crab and lobster are the main UK gear in the study area (MMO, 2025). The whelk fishery in 27.7.d has grown substantially since the mid-2010s, driven by Asian export demand (MMO, 2023).

### Historical effort trends and structural change

Total fishing effort in the Channel has declined substantially since the early 2000s, consistent with EU fleet capacity reduction programmes and quota restrictions under successive CFP reforms. The AER series (2008–2023) shows a general downward trend in fishing days for bottom trawl/seine and beam trawl across all major countries (`r fig_nums("effort_gear_cat", display="cite")`), with the Dutch flyshoot fleet being an important exception showing growth through the 2010s before stabilising post-2020. This is consistent with Quirijns et al. (2020) and STECF (2025a).

Post-Brexit disruption from 2021 onwards has reshaped fleet access in the eastern Channel. UK licensing restrictions have reduced French, Belgian and Dutch access to UK waters in 27.7.d/e, driving spatial redistribution towards French EEZ waters (Phillipson & Symes, 2018; House of Lords, 2022). This structural shift may contribute to the apparent changes in spatial effort patterns visible in the GFW KDE maps (`r fig_nums("kde_all", display="cite")`) around 2021–2022, with effort concentrating in the southern (French EEZ) portion of 27.7.d. Post-Brexit bilateral agreements and access negotiations between the EU member states and the UK continue to shape fleet access patterns in the Channel.

The GFW spatial concentration metrics (`r fig_nums("concentration", display="cite")`) quantify whether this redistribution has led to more or less concentrated effort patterns over time. An increase in Gini coefficient and top-10% share after 2021 is consistent with effort being pushed into a narrower range of spatial locations following access restrictions.

### Stock status of key target species

`r tab_nums("stock_status", display="cite")` summarises the assessment and advice status for the principal commercial stocks in the study area. Stocks are grouped by the ICES working group responsible for their assessment. Note that several species caught in the Channel, particularly cephalopods, do not have formal ICES assessments or TAC-based management; these are indicated accordingly.

```{r stock-status-table, echo=FALSE}
stock_status <- readxl::read_excel(stock_status_file, sheet = "Stock status")

stock_status |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  flextable::italic(j = 1, part = "body") |>
  flextable::merge_v(j = c(1, 2)) |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 7) |>
  flextable::set_caption(caption = tab_nums("stock_status"))

```


### Ecosystem effects and sustainability

The seabed disturbance footprint of the Channel fisheries has been extensively studied. Eigaard et al. (2017) quantified the swept-area ratio across European shelf fisheries and identified the Channel as one of the most intensively bottom-trawled areas in European waters, with beam trawl having the highest physical impact per unit effort. Comparisons between gear types consistently show that Danish seine (flyshoot) has a substantially lower seabed disturbance footprint than comparable otter trawls or beam trawls, primarily because it does not drag heavy groundgear across the seabed in the same manner (Depestele et al., 2016; Hiddink et al., 2017) **[CHECK: Depestele et al. (2016) compares beam and pulse trawls, not seines]**.

Bycatch and discards in the Channel mixed fisheries remain a management concern under the EU landing obligation (in force since 2019), though exemptions for high-survival species and *de minimis* provisions have reduced the practical scope of the obligation for many fleets (ICES WGCSE, 2025a). The flyshoot fishery is generally considered to have moderate bycatch rates compared to other demersal gears, though species composition of the bycatch varies considerably with area and season (Quirijns et al., 2020).


# Discussion & Synthesis

## Effort trends and fleet position

Total fishing effort in the Channel (`r study_area_lab`) has declined substantially over the `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` period covered by the AER series, with a reduction of approximately 30% across all gears and countries combined **[CHECK: recompute; GBR is included up to 2020 only]**. This decline is consistent with the long-term trend of EU fleet capacity reduction under successive CFP reform cycles, and with the structural contraction of the Belgian and Dutch beam trawl segments visible in both landings and effort data. France dominates the total effort picture throughout, contributing around 80% of fishing days **[CHECK: recompute]**, and its otter trawl (OTB) fleet in the eastern Channel shows a steady but gradual decline over the period. Landings of key species have also declined: flatfish landings fell by over 60% since 2008, consistent with poor stock status for Channel sole and plaice, while scallop landings increased markedly since 2016. The FDI-based gear disaggregation, which is only available from 2013 onwards, shows that within the declining bottom trawl/seine category the gear composition has remained broadly stable over the 2013–2023 sub-period.

The Dutch flyshoot (SSC/SDN) fleet presents a contrasting trajectory: although small in absolute days relative to the French OTB fleet, it has been relatively stable and seine-dominated, with the FDI gear split confirming that roughly 70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days in the Channel are attributable to seine gears. This fleet segment is small in AER terms but disproportionately visible in the GFW spatial data because of the high AIS coverage on the larger vessel segments.

Post-Brexit restructuring from 2021 onwards has had a measurable effect on spatial distribution. The GFW annual maps show a progressive reduction in UK effort in 27.7.e and a sharpening of national spatial separation from 2021, consistent with altered access conditions under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement (European Commission, 2021). 

## Contribution of the UK fleet

The MMO data show that the UK and Channel Islands fleets are a substantial user of the study area, accounting for around `r uk_share_pct`% of total landings over `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`. Their fishery profile differs clearly from that of the EU fleets: UK landings are dominated by shellfish taken with pots and traps and dredges, whereas EU landings are dominated by pelagic fish, seaweeds, flatfish and scallops. An analysis based on the AER alone therefore not only underestimates total landings, but also gives a biased picture of the species and gear composition of the fisheries in the study area. The UK data also show substantial demersal seine (flyshoot) landings in 27.7.d.

UK effort is available from the AER up to `r aer_uk_years_end`, but not for the years after, so the post-Brexit fishing pressure of UK vessels cannot be expressed in fishing days. The GFW data suggest that UK vessels account for roughly 25–30% of AIS-derived fishing days, which is of the same order as their share of landings. 

## Comparison of AER and GFW effort metrics

The AER and GFW series measure effort using fundamentally different methodologies: administrative logbook declarations versus AIS-derived vessel-day estimates. Therefore, they are not directly comparable in absolute terms. The GFW series shows an increasing trend from 53,000 to 90,000 days over 2013–2025, while the AER shows a declining trend over 2013–2023. These opposing directions are reconciled by three structural factors: 1) improving AIS coverage over the early years of the GFW series inflates apparent growth; 2) GFW includes the UK effort (contributing ~25–30% of total days); and 3) GFW captures large vessels with high AIS compliance most accurately, while the AER captures the full administrative fleet including small inshore vessels below the AIS carriage threshold.

The most useful role of the GFW data in this report is therefore not as an independent cross-check of absolute effort levels, but as a source of spatial resolution unavailable from the AER. The within-division distribution of effort, the identification of national fishing grounds, and the detection of temporal shifts in spatial patterns can be based on GFW data. Used in this complementary way, the two sources are mutually reinforcing: the AER provides the authoritative time series of effort and landings by fleet segment, while GFW provides the spatial context that the AER cannot. The FDI was retained for the methodologically important role of gear-code disaggregation of the AER bottom trawl/seine category, but its quality limitations (confidentiality suppression, EU-aggregated landings) precluded its use as a primary effort or landings source (STECF, 2025b).

## Compliance with management measures and bilateral agreements

Direct assessment of compliance with effort and gear management measures is beyond the scope of this report, which relies on aggregated AER and GFW data rather than vessel-level logbook or VMS records. However, the data presented allow some observations relevant to the monitoring context. The GFW spatial concentration metrics for `r conc_area_lab` show a step increase in Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share from 2018–2020 onwards **[CHECK: against the values in Section `r sec["concentration"]`]**, which coincides with the period of increasing negotiation pressure around Brexit access arrangements. This pattern is consistent with a progressive restriction of vessel access to previously used grounds, whether through formal licensing or informal avoidance. The partial reduction in concentration since 2022 may reflect stabilisation of access arrangements under the TCA, though concentration remains structurally elevated above pre-2018 levels.

The FDI gear split confirms that the Dutch fleet's contribution to bottom trawl/seine effort in the Channel is predominantly seine (*flyshoot*), providing a quantitative baseline against which future changes in gear composition — for example in response to gear specifications in bilateral agreements — could be assessed. Across all fleets, conventional bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 57% of bottom trawl/seine fishing days, with seine (SSC/SDN) accounting for around 10%, reflecting the much larger scale of the French OTB fleet relative to the Dutch seine fleet. More granular vessel-level monitoring would be required to assess day-level compliance with any sea-day limits. The AER and GFW data presented here operate at fleet-segment and annual resolution and are best suited to detecting structural trends rather than real-time compliance monitoring.

# Conclusions & Recommendations

## Conclusions

This report has characterised fishing effort, landings and spatial distribution in the English Channel (`r study_area_lab`) over the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (AER; UK fleet up to `r aer_uk_years_end`), `r aer_split_years_start`–`r aer_years_end` (FDI), `r min(uk_years)`–`r max(uk_years)` (UK landings, MMO) and `r gfw_years_start`–`r max(study_years)` (GFW), integrating four complementary data sources.

Total fishing effort has declined by approximately 30% since 2008 **[CHECK: recompute]**, driven primarily by contraction of French otter trawl and Belgian and Dutch beam trawl effort. France dominates total effort throughout, contributing around 80% of AER fishing days. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute days, is the dominant seine fleet in the area and has remained relatively stable. UK effort is included up to `r aer_uk_years_end` only; after that the effort trends refer to EU fleets only.

Landings are dominated by flatfishes and scallops; flatfish landings have declined markedly, consistent with the deteriorating stock status of Channel sole and plaice (ICES, 2025a; ICES, 2025b). Scallop landings show an increasing trend since 2016, supported by record biomass in the Baie de Seine (Varenne & Foucher, 2025). UK and Channel Islands vessels accounted for around `r uk_share_pct`% of total landings in the study area over `r min(combined_years)`–`r max(combined_years)`, with a fishery profile centred on shellfish (whelk, scallops, cockles and crab) taken by pots and traps and dredges. Including the UK increases total landings by roughly 20% relative to the EU fleets alone **[CHECK: recompute]** and shifts the overall species composition towards shellfish and crustaceans.

GFW spatial analysis reveals persistent fishing hotspots in the Pas de Calais and Baie de Seine. Post-Brexit spatial restructuring is visible from 2021, with declining UK effort in 27.7.e and increased spatial separation between national fleets. Spatial concentration in `r conc_area_lab` — as measured by the Gini coefficient (`r conc_gini_early` in `r conc_early_lab`, `r conc_gini_late` in `r conc_late_lab`) and top-10% cell share — has increased from a pre-2018 baseline and remains elevated, pointing to a structural rather than temporary shift in spatial behaviour **[CHECK: interpretation]**.

The FDI-based gear-code disaggregation shows that across all fleets, conventional bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 57% of bottom trawl/seine fishing days in the study area, with seine gears (SSC/SDN, predominantly Dutch) accounting for around 10%. The Dutch fleet is distinct in being predominantly seine-dominated (~70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days), while the French fleet is almost entirely OTB (~96%). This baseline characterisation provides the quantitative foundation against which future fleet developments and the effects of access agreements can be assessed.

## Recommendations

1. **Obtain post-Brexit UK effort data.** The most important gap in this analysis is the absence of UK fishing effort after `r aer_uk_years_end`. UK effort data (fishing days, days at sea and kW-days by year, division, gear and vessel length, `r aer_uk_years_end + 1`–2025) should be requested from the MMO, so that the UK fleet can be included in the effort trends after Brexit.
2. **Improve the gear split between otter trawl and seine.** The FDI-based split is limited by confidentiality suppression. Unsuppressed FDI data, or national logbook data by gear code, should be requested from the relevant Member States (in particular France and the Netherlands) to make the split of the AER bottom trawl/seine category more robust.
3. **Update the series when new data become available.** The AER series should be extended to 2024 once French data are published, and the UK series once the MMO publishes 2025 data.

## Annex B — Cache files

Cache files are stored in `output/cache/`r study_area_id`/` (one folder per study area) and are rebuilt automatically when their source data are newer or when objects are missing. Delete any file to force a rebuild on the next knit.

| File | Contents | Rebuilt when |
|------|----------|--------------|
| `cache_divisions.RData` | `fao_sf_division`, `fao_sf_context` | `fao_sf.RData` is newer |
| `cache_aer.RData` | `aer_effort_bysource`, `aer_landings_bysource`, `aer_effort_raw`, `aer_effort_summary`, `aer_effort_capacity_metric`, `aer_landings_raw`, `aer_landings_summary` | Any AER Excel file or the divisions cache is newer |
| `cache_fdi.RData` | `fdi_gearcode`, `fdi_catches` | FDI CSV outputs are newer |
| `cache_uk.RData` | `uk_landings_raw`, `uk_landings_summary` | UK Excel file is newer (delete manually after changing the UK mapping functions) |
| `cache_gfw.RData` | `fishing_days_study`, `events_classified_fr`, `vessel_meta`, `world` | Any GFW pipeline `.RData` is newer |
| `cache_gfw_spatial.RData` | Projected layers, KDE grids, gridded effort, concentration metrics (`concentration_7d`, `concentration_full`) | `cache_gfw.RData` or the divisions cache is newer |
| `cache_aer_split.RData` | `aer_split` | `cache_aer.RData` or `cache_fdi.RData` is newer |
| `cache_map.RData` | `bathy_df` (NOAA depth grid) | The map window (`map_xlim`, `map_ylim`) changes |
| `cache_eez.RData` | `eez_lines` (EEZ boundaries) | Delete manually to download again |

## Annex C — Code section index

The table below maps each figure and table in the report to the R code chunk that generated it and the data it is based on. Figure and table numbers and section numbers are filled in automatically. Chunk names refer to this Rmd file; the data reading functions are in `Channel_fisheries_functions.R`.

Development of the R analysis code and report structure was supported in part by Claude (Anthropic), a large language model AI assistant. The AI assisted with data processing pipeline development, figure code, and drafting of text sections. All analytical decisions, interpretations and conclusions are the responsibility of the author.

```{r annex-c-code-index, echo=FALSE}
# One row per figure or table: captioner key, section key (sec), chunk, data.
# Add a row here when a figure or table is added to the report.
code_index <- tibble::tribble(
  ~type,    ~key,                   ~section,          ~chunk,                                 ~data,
  "Figure", "study_area",           "study_area",      "study-area-map",                       "fao_sf_context, NOAA ETOPO (cache_map), EEZ (cache_eez)",
  "Figure", "data_overview",        "methods",         "data-overview",                        "Hard-coded description of the sources",
  "Table",  "vlc_table",            "vlc",             "vlc-table",                            "Hard-coded",
  "Table",  "spp_group_table",      "spp",             "spp-group-table",                      "Hard-coded",
  "Table",  "uk_gear_map",          "uk",              "uk-gear-map-table",                    "Hard-coded",
  "Figure", "landings_top20",       "landings_top",    "aer-landings-top-species",             "landings_combined (AER + MMO)",
  "Figure", "landings_gear",        "landings_gear",   "aer-landings-total",                   "landings_combined (AER + MMO)",
  "Figure", "landings_spp_grp_cty", "landings_om",     "aer-landings-species-country-groups",  "landings_combined (AER + MMO)",
  "Figure", "landings_spp_cty",     "landings_cty",    "aer-landings-species-country",         "landings_combined (AER + MMO)",
  "Figure", "landings_spp_gear",    "landings_spgear", "aer-landings-species-gear",            "landings_combined (AER + MMO)",
  "Figure", "effort_country",       "effort_country",  "aer-effort-country-total",             "aer_effort_summary (cache_aer)",
  "Figure", "effort_gear_cat",      "effort_gearcat",  "aer-effort-gear-cat",                  "aer_effort_summary (cache_aer)",
  "Figure", "effort_gear",          "effort_vlc",      "aer-effort-trend",                     "aer_effort_summary (cache_aer)",
  "Figure", "effort_size",          "effort_size",     "aer-effort-size-total",                "aer_effort_raw (cache_aer)",
  "Figure", "effort_gt",            "effort_gt",       "aer-effort-gt",                        "aer_effort_raw (cache_aer)",
  "Figure", "split_total",          "split",           "aer-split-trend",                      "aer_split (cache_aer_split)",
  "Figure", "split_fra_nld",        "split",           "aer-split-fra-nld-bars",               "aer_split (cache_aer_split)",
  "Figure", "gfw_flag_total",       "gfw_total",       "gfw-plot-flag-total",                  "fishing_days_study (cache_gfw)",
  "Figure", "aer_gfw_compare",      "gfw_compare",     "aer-gfw-comparison",                   "aer_effort_summary + fishing_days_study",
  "Figure", "gfw_events_all",       "gfw_events",      "gfw-plot-spatial-all",                 "events_classified_fr, vessel_meta (cache_gfw)",
  "Figure", "gfw_events_year",      "gfw_events_yr",   "gfw-plot-spatial-by-year",             "events_classified_fr, vessel_meta (cache_gfw)",
  "Figure", "kde_all",              "kde",             "gfw-plot-kde",                         "kde_results (cache_gfw_spatial)",
  "Figure", "concentration",        "concentration",   "gfw-plot-concentration",               paste0(if (conc_scope == "full") "concentration_full" else "concentration_7d", " (cache_gfw_spatial)"),
  "Table",  "stock_status",         "stock_status",    "stock-status-table",                   "stock_status.xlsx (ICES 2025a\u2013e, literature)"
)

# Figure / table number from the captioners; section number from sec
code_index$number <- NA_character_
for (i in seq_len(nrow(code_index))) {
  if (code_index$type[i] == "Figure") {
    code_index$number[i] <- fig_nums(code_index$key[i], display = "cite")
  } else {
    code_index$number[i] <- tab_nums(code_index$key[i], display = "cite")
  }
}
code_index$section <- unname(sec[code_index$section])

code_index |>
  dplyr::select(`Figure / table` = number, Section = section,
                `Code chunk` = chunk, `Source data` = data) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft_plain(font_size = 8) |>
  flextable::set_caption(caption = tab_nums("code_index",
    "Figures and tables in the report, with the code chunk and the data that generate them."))
```

**KDE computation** (`kde_results`, `kde_7d`): derived in the `load-gfw-spatial` chunk (function `build_gfw_spatial()`) using `spatstat::density.ppp()` with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km (whole study area) and σ = `r sigma_7d/1000` km (`r focus_div_lab`; not shown in this report). Inputs are fishing event coordinates from `events_classified_fr`, sampled to `r kde_sample` events per year.

**Concentration metrics** (`concentration_full`, `concentration_7d`): derived in `load-gfw-spatial` by aggregating events to a `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid covering the whole study area (`concentration_full`) or `r focus_div_lab` (`concentration_7d`), then computing the Gini coefficient (`ineq::Gini()`) and top-10% cell share per year.

**GFW pipeline scripts** (not part of this Rmd — run separately to regenerate the raw `.RData` files in `flyshootdir`):

| Script / Rmd | Purpose | Output file |
|---|---|---|
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` sections 1–3 | Vessel discovery and metadata | `gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData` |
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` sections 4–6 | Event retrieval and zone classification | `gfw_s6_zones.RData` |
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` section 7 | Effort aggregation to vessel-days | `gfw_s7_effort.RData` |
| `AER_channel_analysis.R` | AER exploration and QA plots | (diagnostic output only) |
| `FDI_channel_analysis.R` | FDI loading, cleaning, QA | `fdi_fishingdays_*.csv`, `fdi_catches_*.csv` |

```{r annex-d6, echo=FALSE}

  make_annex_table(
    df         = aer_split |>
                   filter(split_source == "FDI direct",
                          year         %in% aer_split_years_start:aer_years_end),
    row_var    = "year",  col_var   = "gear_type",

```


Bottom trawl/seine disaggregated into bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) using FDI split key. Other focused gears shown as reported in AER.

```{r annex-d7, echo=FALSE}
# Years before the FDI split is available: bottom trawl/seine unsplit
pre_split_years  <- aer_years_start:(aer_split_years_start - 1)
post_split_years <- aer_split_years_start:aer_years_end

gear_order <- c("Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)",
                "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)",
                "Seine (SSC/SDN)",
                setdiff(capacity_gears, "Bottom trawl/seine"))

# Block 1: before the FDI split — BTS unsplit, other gears normal
pre2013_bts <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% pre_split_years) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category) |>
  mutate(gear_label = "Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)")

pre2013_other <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         gear_category != "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% pre_split_years) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category)

# Block 2: from the FDI split onwards — BTS split via FDI, other gears normal
post2013_bts <- if (!is.null(aer_split)) {
  aer_split |>
    filter(year      %in% post_split_years,
           gear_type != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    rename(gear_label = gear_type)
} else {
  aer_effort_summary |>
    filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
           gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
           year          %in% post_split_years) |>
    group_by(year, gear_category) |>
    summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    rename(gear_label = gear_category) |>
    mutate(gear_label = "Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)")
}

post2013_other <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         gear_category != "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% post_split_years) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category)

all_data <- bind_rows(pre2013_bts, pre2013_other,
                      post2013_bts, post2013_other) |>
  mutate(totfishdays = round(totfishdays)) |>
  group_by(year, gear_label) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from  = gear_label,
              values_from = totfishdays,
              values_fill = NA) |>
  dplyr::select(year, any_of(gear_order)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(any_of(gear_order)), na.rm=TRUE))

# Build total row separately on the completed data frame
total_row <- all_data |>
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) sum(x, na.rm=TRUE))) |>
  mutate(year = NA_integer_)

# Bind and convert year to character
all_data <- bind_rows(all_data, total_row) |>
  mutate(year = if_else(is.na(year), "Total", as.character(year)))

# Convert NA to "--" for display (must be character columns)
all_data_display <- all_data |>
  mutate(across(any_of(gear_order),
                \(x) if_else(is.na(x), "--", formatC(x, format="d", big.mark=","))))

# Rename year column
names(all_data_display)[1] <- "Year"

# Build flextable
ft <- flextable::flextable(all_data_display) |>
  style_ft(font_size = 8) |>
  # Right-align numeric-looking columns (all except Year)
  flextable::align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 1,  align = "left",  part = "all") |>
  # Shade the years before the FDI split slightly to signal the unsplit period
  flextable::bg(i = ~ Year %in% as.character(pre_split_years),
                j = c("Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)", "Seine (SSC/SDN)"),
                bg = "#EEEEEE") |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = annex_tab("annex_d7",
      paste0("Total fishing days by year and gear, with bottom trawl/seine ",
             "disaggregated using the FDI gear-code split from ", aer_split_years_start, " onwards. ",
             "'--' indicates gear not separately reported for that year. ",
             study_area_lab, " (AER + FDI, ",
             aer_years_start, "\u2013", aer_years_end, ")."))
  )

ft
```
